He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]] and was drafted by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the 38th overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. Between 2011 and 2020, Parsons played in the NBA for the Rockets, [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Memphis Grizzlies]], and [[Atlanta Hawks]] before injuries caused by a drunk driver forced him into retirement. Post-retirement, he became a sports commentator, including currently as the co-host of [[FanDuel]] online show ''Run It Back''. ==Early life== Parsons was born in [[Casselberry, Florida]], and attended [[Lake Howell High School]] alongside future fellow Florida Gator [[Nick Calathes]]. Together, Parsons and Calathes helped the Lake Howell Silverhawks [[basketball#High school basketball|high school basketball]] team advance to the Florida Class 5A state basketball championship final four in 2005, 2006 and 2007, winning the state championship in 2007. As a senior, Parsons was a first-team all-state selection, and was recognized as the most valuable player of the state championship game after scoring thirty points and grabbing ten rebounds.{{cite web | url=http://floridagators.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=538 | title=25 Chandler Parsons | work=floridagators.com | access-date=November 28, 2017}} ==College career== Parsons accepted an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of Florida]] in Gainesville, Florida, where he played for coach [[Billy Donovan]]'s [[Florida Gators men's basketball]] team from [[2007–08 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2007]] to [[2010–11 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2011]]. Parsons commented that playing for four years under Donovan gave him an advantage over other players who left the team early.{{cite news|last=Brockway|first=Kevin|title=Parsons says staying in school helped in NBA|url=http://www.gainesville.com/article/20120609/ARTICLES/120609612|work=Gainesville.com|date=June 9, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029185344/http://www.gainesville.com/article/20120609/ARTICLES/120609612?p=all&tc=pgall|archive-date=October 29, 2013|url-status=dead}} During his freshman season, Parsons played in 36 games averaging 8.1 points per game and 4.0 rebounds per game, but the Gators failed to make the NCAA Tournament. During the 2008–09 season, Parsons saw more playing time and his scoring, rebounding, and assists all improved. The Gators once again failed to make the NCAA tournament, though. In his junior season, Parsons averaged 12.4 points, 6.9 rebounds, and 2.6 assists per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/chandler-parsons-1.html|title=Chandler Parsons College Stats|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com}} On January 3, 2010, Parsons hit a 75-foot shot with no time left in overtime to give the Gators a one-point victory over North Carolina State.{{cite news|url=http://www.gatorzone.com/story.php?id=17186|title=Parsons' Buzzer Beater Downs N.C. State, 62-61|date=January 3, 2010|work=GatorZone.com|access-date=December 21, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131030072305/http://www.gatorzone.com/story.php?id=17186|archive-date=October 30, 2013|url-status=dead}} The Gators were invited to the [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]], but lost to [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] in the first round. During the 2010–11 season, Parsons averaged 11.3 points and 7.8 rebounds in 34.1 minutes per game while leading the Gators to the best regular-season record in the SEC. On January 23, 2011, the Gators trailed South Carolina by one when Parsons hit a three-point shot to give the Gators the win.{{cite news|url=http://www.gatorzone.com/story.php?id=17302|title=Parsons' Buzzer Beater Leads UF Over South Carolina, 58-56|date=January 23, 2010|work=GatorZone.com|access-date=December 21, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131030001521/http://www.gatorzone.com/story.php?id=17302|archive-date=October 30, 2013|url-status=dead}} On March 8, 2011, he was named the 2011 [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]], becoming the first Florida Gator to win that honor.{{cite news|url=http://www.tampabay.com/blogs/gators/content/billy-donovan-chandler-parsons-named-sec-coach-and-player-year|title=Billy Donovan, Chandler Parsons named SEC Coach and Player of the Year|first=Antonya|last=English|date=March 8, 2011|work=TampaBay.com|access-date=January 1, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150101214402/http://www.tampabay.com/blogs/gators/content/billy-donovan-chandler-parsons-named-sec-coach-and-player-year|archive-date=January 1, 2015|url-status=dead}} The Gators also made the NCAA Tournament for the second year in a row. In the first three rounds of the tournament, the Gators beat [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], and [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]]. In the Elite Eight, the Gators lost to [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]]. Parsons was picked to the All-America fifth team by [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]].{{cite news|first=Jeff |last=Goodman |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |title=Goodman's 2010-11 All-America teams |work=FoxSports.com |url-status=dead }} ===Houston Rockets (2011–2014)=== Parsons signed with the Rockets on December 18, 2011.{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=8874 |title=Rockets sign 2nd round pick |archive-date=October 16, 2012 |url-status=dead }} In the Rockets' season finale on April 22, 2012, Parsons scored a season-high 23 points against the [[Miami Heat]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/parsoch01/gamelog/2012/ |title=Chandler Parsons 2011-12 Game Log |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=November 4, 2018}} For the season, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]].{{cite web|title=Irving, Rubio headline 2011-12 NBA All-Rookie First Team|url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/05/22/all-rookie-team-release/index.html|work=NBA.com|date=May 22, 2012|access-date=May 23, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525095317/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/05/22/all-rookie-team-release/index.html|archive-date=May 25, 2012|url-status=dead}} On November 12, 2012, Parsons scored a career-high 25 points against the Heat.{{Cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/parsoch01/gamelog/2013/ |title=Chandler Parsons 2012-13 Game Log |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=November 4, 2018}} On November 23, he set a new career high with 31 points against the [[New York Knicks]]. On March 3, 2013, Parsons scored a career-high 32 points on 12-for-13 shooting in a 136–103 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400278605|title=Chandler Parsons nets 32 points as Rockets end skid vs. Mavs|work=ESPN.com|date=March 3, 2013|access-date=November 4, 2018}} On January 24, 2014, Parsons scored a career-high 34 points and made 10 3-pointers—all in the second half—in an 88–87 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. He set an NBA record for 3s in a half and a franchise record for 3s in a game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400489515|title=Chandler Parsons sets record with 10 3s in half in loss to Grizzlies|work=ESPN.com|date=January 24, 2014|access-date=November 4, 2018}}{{cite web|last=Fromal|first=Adam|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1936031-chandler-parsons-sets-rockets-team-record-with-10-3-pointers-all-in-2nd-half|title=Chandler Parsons Hits 10 Threes in 1 Half, Sets NBA Record|work=BleacherReport.com|date=January 24, 2014|access-date=January 25, 2014}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2014–2016)=== [[File:20141119 Washington Wizards vs Dallas Mavericks.jpg|thumb|left|Parsons (#25) with the Mavericks in November 2014]] After the 2013–14 season, Parsons became a [[restricted free agent (NBA)|restricted free agent]]. On July 10, 2014, he received a three-year, $46 million offer sheet from the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2014/07/chandler-parsons-agrees.html|title=Mavs, Rockets Talk Parsons Sign-And-Trade|website=Hoops Rumors|date=July 10, 2014 }}{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234213/Mavs-Submit-Chandler-Parsons-Offer-Sheet-To-Rockets|title=Mavs Submit Chandler Parsons Offer Sheet To Rockets|website=basketball.realgm.com}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2014/07/10/chandler-parsons-houston-rockets-qualifying-offer-match-dallas-mavericks/12488109/|title=Rockets on clock for Mavericks' Chandler Parsons offer|first=Sam|last=Amick|website=USA TODAY}} The Rockets declined to match the offer{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/dallas/nba/story/_/id/11211261/houston-rockets-decline-match-dallas-mavericks-offer-chandler-parsons|title=Chandler Parsons to play for Mavs|last=Goodman|first=Jeff|publisher=ESPN|date=July 14, 2014|access-date=October 26, 2014}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/07/13/parsons-to-mavericks.ap/index.html|title=Parsons headed to Mavs; Rockets not matching offer|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2014|access-date=October 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150111192710/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/07/13/parsons-to-mavericks.ap/index.html|archive-date=January 11, 2015|url-status=dead}} and Parsons signed with the Mavericks on July 15.{{cite web|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-chandler-parsons/|title=Mavericks Sign Chandler Parsons|work=Mavs.com|date=July 15, 2014|access-date=October 26, 2014}} On December 17, 2014, Parsons scored a season-high 32 points against the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/parsoch01/gamelog/2015/ |title=Chandler Parsons 2014-15 Game Log |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=November 4, 2018}} On March 8, 2015, Parsons returned to action against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] after a seven-game absence with a sprained left ankle.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150308/DALLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Ellis' big 3rd quarter helps Mavericks beat Lakers 100-93|work=NBA.com|date=March 8, 2015|access-date=March 9, 2015}} Parsons missed the final six regular-season games due to a right knee injury.{{cite web|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavs-begin-moving-forward-minus-chandler-parsons-rajon-rondo/|title=Mavs begin moving forward minus Chandler Parsons, Rajon Rondo|work=mavs.com|date=April 22, 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518101214/http://www.mavs.com/mavs-begin-moving-forward-minus-chandler-parsons-rajon-rondo/|archive-date=May 18, 2015}} He played in game one of the Mavericks' first-round playoff series against the Rockets, then missed the rest of the series with the same knee injury. He subsequently had knee surgery on May 1.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/2015/9/28/9408481/chandler-parsons-knee-surgery-revealed-injury-dallas-mavericks|title=Parsons' mysterious knee surgery finally revealed|first=Tim|last=Cato|date=September 28, 2015|website=SBNation.com}} Parsons returned to action in the third game of the 2015–16 season,{{Cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/parsoch01/gamelog/2016/ |title=Chandler Parsons 2015-16 Game Log |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=November 4, 2018}} then dealt with strict minutes restrictions for the first six weeks of the season.{{cite web|last=MacMahon|first=Tim|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/15065520/chandler-parsons-dallas-mavericks-surgery-repair-torn-meniscus-right-knee|title=Chandler Parsons has surgery to repair torn meniscus|work=ESPN.com|date=March 26, 2016|access-date=November 4, 2018}} On January 24, 2016, he scored a season-high 31 points in a 115–104 loss to the Rockets.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160124/DALHOU/gameinfo.html |title=Harden's triple-double leads Rockets over Mavericks 115-104 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 25, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181226205346/http://www.nba.com/games/20160124/DALHOU/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 26, 2018 |url-status=dead }} On March 25, he underwent successful surgery to address the torn meniscus in his right knee, ruling him out for the rest of the season.{{cite web|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-forward-chandler-parsons-undergoes-right-knee-surgery/|title=Mavericks forward Chandler Parsons undergoes right knee surgery|work=mavs.com|date=March 25, 2016|access-date=March 25, 2016}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2016–2019)=== On July 7, 2016, Parsons signed a four-year, $94 million contract with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/chandler-parsons-signed-160707|title=Grizzlies sign Chandler Parsons to multi-year contract|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2016|access-date=July 7, 2016}} Heading into training camp, Parsons was on light duties coming off knee surgery.{{cite web|last=Calkins|first=Geoff|url=http://www.commercialappeal.com/sports/grizzlies/great-things-possible-if-grizzlies-stay-healthy-3d6b4480-3d0a-6d5d-e053-0100007fbaa6-394875841.html|title=Great things possible, if Grizzlies stay healthy|work=CommercialAppeal.com|date=September 26, 2016|access-date=September 28, 2016}} He did not play in the preseason or in the first six games of the regular season. On November 6, he made his debut for the Grizzlies against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], but in 22 minutes as a starter, he missed all eight of his field goals attempts.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899538|title=McCollum matches career high, Blazers beat Grizzlies 100-94|work=ESPN.com|date=November 6, 2016|access-date=November 6, 2016}} He appeared in six games for the Grizzlies before missing the next 17 with a bone bruise on his left knee, making his return to the line-up on December 21 against the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899873|title=Gasol ties career high with 38, Grizzlies beat Pistons 98-86|work=ESPN.com|date=December 21, 2016|access-date=December 22, 2016}} On March 13, 2017, he was ruled out indefinitely after he was diagnosed with a partial tear of the meniscus in his left knee.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/parsons-medical-update-170313|title=Chandler Parsons medical update|work=NBA.com|date=March 13, 2017|access-date=March 13, 2017}} He subsequently missed the rest of the season with a third knee injury in three years.{{cite web|last=Cato|first=Tim|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2017/3/13/14916882/chandler-parsons-injury-knee-partial-meniscus-tear-grizzlies|title=Chandler Parsons suffers partial meniscus tear, his 3rd knee injury in 3 years|work=sbnation.com|date=March 13, 2017|access-date=November 4, 2018}} On October 28, 2017, Parsons scored 24 points on 9 of 11 from the field and 6 of 8 from 3-point range in a 103–89 win over the [[Houston Rockets]]. Parsons' 24 points were his best in 39 games with Memphis.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974831|title=Parsons, Grizzlies' bench leads Memphis past Houston|work=ESPN.com|date=October 28, 2017|access-date=October 29, 2017}} Chandler had an extended stint on the sidelines between late December and mid-February due to right knee soreness.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975607|title=George, Westbrook's triple-double lead OKC past Grizzlies|work=ESPN.com|date=February 14, 2018|access-date=February 14, 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/parsoch01/gamelog/2018/|title=Chandler Parsons 2017-18 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 14, 2018}} Despite only appearing in 36 games during the 2017–18 season, Parsons shot a career-best 42% from 3-point range.{{cite web|last=Ratliff|first=Greg|url=https://www.grizzlybearblues.com/2018/10/5/17940018/memphis-grizzlies-2018-19-player-preview-chandler-parsons-nba|title=Memphis Grizzlies 2018-19 Player Preview: Chandler Parsons|work=grizzlybearblues.com|date=October 5, 2018|access-date=November 4, 2018}} Parsons earned a starting spot for the 2018–19 season out of training camp,{{cite web|last1=Wojnarowski|first1=Adrian|last2=MacMahon|first2=Tim|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/25699385/chandler-parsons-memphis-grizzlies-agree-part-ways|title=Chandler Parsons, Memphis Grizzlies agree to part ways|work=ESPN.com|date=January 6, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2019}} but only played in the first three games before being sidelined with right knee soreness.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070828|title=Warriors use big third quarter to beat Grizzlies 117-101|work=ESPN.com|date=November 5, 2018|access-date=November 5, 2018|quote=...F Chandler Parsons sat his sixth consecutive contest because of a sore right knee.}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071177|title=Grizzlies end 5-game skid by beating Lakers 107-99|work=ESPN.com|date=December 23, 2018|access-date=December 24, 2018|quote=Parsons has missed 30 games because of soreness in his right knee.}} By the close of December, Parsons was still sidelined by order of the organization despite having been medically cleared to return on December 21.{{cite web|last=Giannotto|first=Mark|url=https://eu.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/columnists/mark-giannotto/2018/12/29/chandler-parsons-injury-memphis-grizzlies-nba/2421430002/|title=Exclusive: Chandler Parsons says he's ready to play in NBA but that Memphis Grizzlies won't let him|work=commercialappeal.com|date=December 29, 2018|access-date=December 30, 2018}} The Grizzlies were keen for Parsons to spend time in the [[NBA G League]] with their affiliate team, the [[Memphis Hustle]], before deciding on returning Parsons to the active roster with the Grizzlies. Parsons had been willing to play in the G League but wanted a clearer plan and a timetable in place that would return him to the Grizzlies' active roster. As a result, on January 6, he left the team indefinitely as the two sides worked to structure a resolution on his future.{{cite news|last=Cobb|first=David|title=Grizzlies GM Chris Wallace on Chandler Parsons: 'Definitely had good information'|date=January 7, 2019|newspaper=Memphis Commercial Appeal|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/2019/01/07/memphis-grizzlies-chandler-parsons-chris-wallace/2448378002/|access-date=January 18, 2019}} On February 9, it was announced that Parsons would return to the Grizzlies after the All-Star break.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2019/02/09/report-chandler-parsons-rejoin-grizzlies|title=Grizzlies' Bickerstaff comments on Chandler Parsons' potential return|work=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2019|access-date=February 9, 2019}} On February 22, after having not played since the third game of the season, Parsons returned to the rotation, playing almost 20 minutes and scoring three points on 1-of-7 shooting in a 112–106 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071552|title=Montrezl Harrell scores 30, Clippers beat Grizzlies 112-106|work=ESPN.com|date=February 22, 2019|access-date=February 22, 2019}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2019–2020)=== On July 6, 2019, Parsons was traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for [[Solomon Hill (basketball)|Solomon Hill]] and [[Miles Plumlee]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-acquire-chandler-parsons-memphis-grizzlies|title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Chandler Parsons From Memphis Grizzlies|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2019}} Parsons was hit by a drunk driver on January 15, 2020; he had appeared in five games with the Hawks before the crash.{{cite web |title=Chandler Parsons Injury Update |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/chandler-parsons-injury-update |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 20, 2020 |date=January 15, 2020}}{{cite web |title=Hawks' Parsons sustains concussion in car wreck |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28492320/hawks-chandler-parsons-diagnosed-concussion-whiplash-car-crash |website=ESPN.com |access-date=January 20, 2020 |date=January 15, 2020}} On January 20, Parsons's attorney announced that his accident-related injuries could be career-ending.{{cite web |title=Hawks' Parsons injured by drunk driver, says firm |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28523841/law-firm-says-hawks-chandler-parsons-injured-drunk-driver |website=ESPN.com |access-date=January 20, 2020 |date=January 20, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Negley |first1=Cassandra |title=Attorney: Hawks' Chandler Parsons suffering from 'permanent' car crash injuries that could end NBA career |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/attorney-hawks-chandler-parsons-suffering-from-permanent-car-crash-injuries-that-could-end-nba-career-173912891.html |website=sports.yahoo.com |access-date=January 20, 2020 |date=January 20, 2020}} On February 5, Parsons was waived by the Hawks.{{cite web |title=Hawks Request Waivers on Chandler Parsons |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-request-waivers-chandler-parsons |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 6, 2020 |date=February 5, 2020}} On January 18, 2022, Parsons announced his retirement from the NBA. He played a total of 440 games in the NBA and averaged 12.7 points, 4.5 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game.{{Cite web|last=Wells|first=Adam|title=Chandler Parsons Retires from NBA; Injury Lawsuit
